complex_scenario: earthquake-aftershock backup ward during a power transfer

reference.role: visible facial and hair appearance guidance for an original adult fictional subject
reference.claim_boundary: No identity, biometric, same-person, ethnicity, nationality, occupation, health, attractiveness, or protected-trait claim.

gates.criterion: The adult subject and workwear first read as a clinical nurse on duty rather than a costume model or generic visitor.
Scrub or tunic-and-trouser components form one coherent practical duty-uniform system with identification placement.
One assessment action is visibly linked to one identifiable patient or patient marker.
The open chart or handover record visibly agrees with the bedside monitor state.
Clinical role relation survives beyond a stethoscope, badge, or hospital backdrop alone.
The primary fictional subject is unambiguously adult-presenting.
The primary subject visibly carries the reference-observed front-facing facial appearance direction and long dark softly waved hair, evaluated as appearance guidance only.
Hands, fingers, gloves, IV-line handling, and equipment contact are physically coherent.
Aftershock disturbance and a simultaneous battery-to-generator lighting transition are both visually legible.
One coherent single-frame nursing action links nurse, patient marker, IV line, monitor, and chart without causal ambiguity.
